label: prf:em-spectral-completeness
title: Proof of em spectral completeness
html:
Proof. The braiding eigenvalue extraction (eigenvalue extraction) shows that c_{A,A} satisfies the Hecke minimal polynomial

  (c_{A,A} - q^{1/2})(c_{A,A} + q^{-1/2}) \;=\; 0

in E. The two eigenvalues q^{1/2}, -q^{-1/2} are distinct (their difference q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2} is a unit in R), so the minimal polynomial splits over R and Bezout produces orthogonal idempotents

  e_- \;=\; \frac{q^{1/2} \cdot \mathrm{id} - c_{A,A}}{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}}
      \;=\; \frac{q \cdot \mathrm{id} - \sigma}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad
  e_+ \;=\; \mathrm{id} - e_-
      \;=\; \frac{\sigma + q^{-1} \cdot \mathrm{id}}{q + q^{-1}},

where \sigma := q^{1/2}\,c_{A,A} satisfies the integer-power Hecke quadratic (\sigma - q)(\sigma + q^{-1}) = 0, i.e. \sigma^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma + 1, over the subring \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}, (q + q^{-1})^{-1}] \subset R. These idempotents are central in E since c_{A,A} (or \sigma) generates the centraliser of the diagonal R-action by Schur--Weyl-Hecke duality. Statement (2) follows from H_2(R, q) \cong E being free of rank 2 over R: E has at most two simple summands, and e_\pm realise them. The singlet identification V_- \cong \mathbf{1} is the standard Schur-functor decomposition A \otimes A = S^2 A \oplus \Lambda^2 A with \Lambda^2 A \cong \mathbf{1} when A is the fundamental of \mathrm{SU}_q(2). Statement (4) follows from (1) and (2): the categorical trace is additive, so \mathrm{tr}_q(e_+) + \mathrm{tr}_q(e_-) = \mathrm{tr}_q(\mathrm{id}_{A \otimes A}) = (\dim_q A)^2 = [2]_q^{\,2}, and \mathrm{tr}_q(e_\pm) = \dim_q V_\pm with \dim_q V_+ = [3]_q, \dim_q V_- = 1. This is the n = 2 case of the Wedderburn trace identity with multiplicities 1. The squared form (\dim_q V_\pm)^2/[2]_q! does not sum to 1: it gives ([3]_q^2 + 1)/[2]_q, which is 5 at q = 1. \square
